sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{State Parseval's identity for Fourier series in } (-L, L).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{For } x^2: a_0 = \frac{2\pi^2}{3}, a_n = \frac{4}{n^2}(-1)^n, b_n=0\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{LHS: } \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} x^4 dx = \frac{\pi^4}{5}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{RHS: } \frac{1}{4}(\frac{2\pi^2}{3})^2 + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (\frac{4}{n^2})^2 = \frac{\pi^4}{9} + 8\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^4}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Equate: } \frac{\pi^4}{5} = \frac{\pi^4}{9} + 8\sum \frac{1}{n^4} \Rightarrow \sum \frac{1}{n^4} = \frac{\pi^4}{90}\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Using Parseval's identity for } f(x)=x^2 \text{ in } (-\pi,\pi), \text{ prove } \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^4} = \frac{\pi^4}{90}.\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\frac{1}{L} \int_0^{L} [f(x)]^2 dx = \frac{a_0^2}{4} + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n^2\)

(4 Mark)

\(\text{where } a_n \text{ are cosine series coefficients}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{For half-range sine series: } \frac{1}{L} \int_0^{L} [f(x)]^2 dx = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n^2\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{State Parseval's identity for half-range cosine series.}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{For } f(x)=x: a_0 = \pi, a_n = \frac{2}{n^2\pi}[(-1)^n-1] = -\frac{4}{n^2\pi} \text{ for odd n}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Parseval: } \frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi} x^2 dx = \frac{\pi^2}{3} = \frac{\pi^2}{4} + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{n=\text{odd}} (\frac{4}{n^2\pi})^2\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Simplify: } \frac{\pi^2}{3} - \frac{\pi^2}{4} = \frac{8}{\pi^2}\sum_{n=\text{odd}} \frac{1}{n^4}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus } \sum_{n=\text{odd}} \frac{1}{n^4} = \frac{\pi^4}{96} \Rightarrow \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^4} = \frac{\pi^4}{90}\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Using half-range cosine series for } f(x)=x \text{ in } (0,\pi), \text{ find } \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^4}.\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{RMS value = } \sqrt{\frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b [f(x)]^2 dx}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{For periodic function with period } 2L: \text{RMS} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{2L}\int_{-L}^L [f(x)]^2 dx}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{From Parseval: RMS}^2 = \frac{a_0^2}{4} + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (a_n^2 + b_n^2)\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus Parseval gives RMS in terms of Fourier coefficients}\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{What is RMS value and how is it related to Parseval's identity?}\)

lq.ANSWER:
StepMarks
Cosine series: \(e^x=\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n\cos n\pi x\)(1)
\(a_0=2\int_0^1 e^x dx=2(e-1)\)(2)
\(a_n=2\int_0^1 e^x\cos n\pi x\,dx=\frac{2(e-1)}{1+n^2\pi^2}\)(4)
Parseval's: \(\int_0^1 e^{2x}dx=\frac{a_0^2}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\sum a_n^2\)(3)
Compute: \(\frac{e^2-1}{2}=\frac{(e-1)^2}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sum\frac{4(e-1)^2}{(1+n^2\pi^2)^2}\) ⇒ \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(1+n^2\pi^2)^2}=\frac{e^2+1}{4(e-1)^2}-\frac{1}{2}\)(5)
